name: Sunsama
description: Sunsama is a guided daily planner that combines tasks, calendars, timeboxing, focus sessions, and work imported from other tools in one deliberate schedule. People use it to plan each day, organize work by channels and weekly objectives, estimate and track focused time, keep a backlog, and review what they accomplished without turning the day into an endless to-do list.
agentUseSummary: Connect a Sunsama account once, then select which agents can read daily tasks and backlog work or manage authorized tasks, notes, estimates, channels, timeboxes, focus, and timers under Safe or Dangerous policy.

capabilities.label: Read daily tasks, backlog, and task details
capabilities.description: Read the authorized task list for a chosen day, ordered backlog tasks, individual task details, notes, estimates, priority, channel and integration-source context exposed by Sunsama.

capabilities.label: Manage tasks, notes, planning, focus, and timers
capabilities.description: Use Sunsama's current live MCP tools to create and edit tasks, assign channels, append or replace notes, change estimates and dates, complete work, timebox tasks, and control supported focus or timer actions.

allowed.label: Read Sunsama
allowed.description: Use one provider-declared read-only Sunsama tool or the bounded daily-task resource with live-schema-validated arguments.

approvalRequired.label: Manage Sunsama
approvalRequired.description: Use one provider-declared task, notes, planning, focus, timer, or other Sunsama mutation; Safe mode requires approval.

blocked.label: Mount raw MCP
blocked.description: Relay exposes typed read and manage wrappers rather than an ungoverned provider tool surface.

blocked.label: Use another MCP origin
blocked.description: OAuth tokens are attached only to Sunsama's published hosted MCP resource.

blocked.label: Expose OAuth credentials
blocked.description: OAuth tokens stay encrypted and never enter agent-visible arguments or results.

blocked.label: Run an unbounded transfer
blocked.description: Relay bounds live schemas, arguments, result sizes, nesting, pagination, redirects, and execution time.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Daily-task resources and provider-declared read-only tools run directly. Every task, planning, notes, focus, timer, or other provider mutation requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: Every selected OAuth-authorized Sunsama operation runs without Relay per-action approval. Connection ownership, provider authority, live schema verification, fixed origin, bounds, credential protection, provider limits, and audits still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway verifies Sunsama's live MCP schemas and mounts bounded read and manage wrappers with refreshed OAuth attached only to the fixed hosted endpoint.
Railway verifies Sunsama's live MCP schemas and mounts bounded read and manage wrappers with refreshed OAuth attached only to the fixed hosted endpoint.

providerSetup.blocker: Relay Console's public S256 PKCE client is dynamically registered with Sunsama and its non-secret client ID is configured on Railway. A signed-in Sunsama subscriber with representative data is still required for production OAuth and MCP acceptance.
providerSetup.nextAction: A Sunsama subscriber clicks Connect, approves read, execute, and offline_access, then Relay verifies callback, rotating refresh tokens, the current complete live tool schema, the daily-task resource, representative reads, Safe mutation denial and approval, Dangerous task and timeboxing management, redaction, upstream revocation, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: Sunsama documents the hosted https://api.sunsama.com/mcp resource, remote OAuth authentication, and direct connection from standards-compatible MCP clients.
Sunsama publishes the exact protected MCP resource, its authorization server, and read, execute, plus offline_access scopes.
Sunsama publishes authorization, token, dynamic-registration and revocation endpoints with authorization-code and refresh grants, public clients, S256 PKCE, and client metadata documents.
Sunsama's official changelog confirms current MCP tools for ordered backlog reads, task-by-ID reads, task creation, task-note editing and appending, and task timeboxing.

Sunsama's official roadmap documents the daily-task resource template, add_task_to_channel, edit_task_estimate, timer and focus support, rotating refresh tokens, early-beta limitations, and the lack of MCP webhooks and actual-time reads.
